newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TV channel no comment on loss report.
newsitem.headline: French TV channel no comment on loss report.

text.p: French public television channel France 2 declined comment on a report in Wednesday's Le Monde newspaper that it would show a loss of at least 70 million francs ($12 million) for 1996.
"We have no comment on this, as it is premature since the accounts have not yet been finalised," a spokesman at France 2 said in answer to Reuters questions.

Le Monde, which appeared on Wednesday afternoon, said France 2 and all the other French public channels, general channel France 3 and specialist stations La Sept, La Cinquieme and Arte, would show losses for 1996 but the financial situation at France 2 was the worst.
It also said the France 2 board had been due to meet on June 7 and will now meet on June 18.
On Monday France 2 managing director Jean-Pierre Cottet, presenting the channel's summer programmes, said France 2 could pull out strong programming if it had more public financing.

France 2, which rivals private channel TF1 for France's top viewing slot, has a 25 percent market share and an annual budget of 4.6 billion francs, of which 52 percent comes from advertising revenue. DT/SLA ($ = 5.821 French Francs)
